field_glossary.backend_ladder: Per-backend outcome of the kernel-agent dispatch. ``produced_artifact=false`` across all rows is the dominant signal that the entire ladder failed for this kernel.
field_glossary.bandwidth: Per-case ``bytes`` / ``algbw_gbps`` / ``busbw_gbps`` from the final bench. Latency alone cannot separate a faster transfer from a cheaper barrier; bus bandwidth against the fabric peak says which one a kept kernel bought, and which regime still has headroom.
field_glossary.bound_type: Whether the kernel is limited by memory bandwidth (memory-bound) or compute (compute-bound).
field_glossary.collective_attempt_id: Stable identity for one collective campaign, used to deduplicate resumed or salvaged attempts across a session.
field_glossary.collective_op: The collective primitive that was optimized: ``all_reduce``, ``reduce_scatter`` or ``all_gather``.
field_glossary.compile_passed: True only if at least one backend in the ladder produced a usable patch. False means the whole backend ladder failed to produce any compiled artifact.
field_glossary.e2e_gain_pct: End-to-end throughput delta measured by the integrate gate. This, not micro_speedup, decides whether a collective KEEP is adopted.
field_glossary.efficiency_pct: Achieved throughput as a percentage of the kernel's roofline peak for its bound_type. Lower = more headroom to gain.
field_glossary.gpu_pct: Share of total GPU time spent in this kernel (kernel_duration / total_gpu_duration). Higher = more impactful to optimize.
field_glossary.lane: Which optimization lane produced the row. ``collective`` rows come from the multi-GPU comm lane and carry no roofline geometry, so efficiency_pct / bound_type / arithmetic_intensity stay null.
field_glossary.salvaged: True when the validated best was recovered from the campaign sidecar after the wrapper timed out, rather than returned by a clean exit.
field_glossary.speedup_basis: Whether the row's headline number was validated end to end (``e2e``) or is a microbenchmark ratio only. A collective's microbenchmark routinely overstates its end-to-end worth, so treat ``microbenchmark`` rows as unproven.
field_glossary.world_size: Rank count the collective was measured across; the lane requires it to match the run's TP width.

new_findings.expected_impact: Turns the dead baseline into a booting server and de-confounds every future kernel-selection variant on this host.
new_findings.what: vLLM 0.28's AOT compile cache does NOT invalidate on kernel-SELECTION changes, so any enablement patch touching the scaled_mm registry is unreproducible on a host with a warm /root/.cache/vllm. The AOT dir hash covers config factors + _model_hash_key(forward) only (decorators.py:537-546) and _verify_source_unchanged re-checks only the traced files recorded by the EXISTING artifact. A patch that edits just the registry __init__ and adds a new kernel module changes neither set, so the pre-patch graph (which hard-codes extern_kernels._scaled_mm on an FP8 [K,N] column-major weight) is replayed against the new BF16 [N,K] row-major weight and dies on inductor's arg guard - the artifact, not the patch, is incompatible. Correct probe: VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1, or better a per-run VLLM_CACHE_ROOT (decorators.py:543-545 reads it).

new_findings.expected_impact: Explains why 0 variants of the baseline config can boot and scopes the fix to exactly one registry insertion point.
new_findings.what: On gfx90a the FP8 registry deterministically selects ChannelWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel and aborts, because gfx90a reports capability (9,0) and the Torch scaled_mm kernels gate on '>= 89'. The aiter FP8 kernels ranked above it are correctly arch-gated off, so the first kernel that passes is one that cannot execute. Engine-level, independent of TP/concurrency/params, and NOT avoidable by any existing --quantization or --linear-backend value ('emulation' maps only to MXFP4/6/8+NVFP4, 'torch' maps exactly to the three aborting kernels, 'triton' has no ROCm bucket so _resolve_backend_kernels warns and falls back) - a source patch is mandatory to close this gap.

new_findings.accuracy_risk: low - E4M3->BF16 is an exact cast (3+1 mantissa / 4-bit exponent fit BF16) and dropping the activation FP8 requant removes one error term versus a true w8a8 scaled GEMM, so this path is expected to be at or slightly ABOVE the FP8 reference in accuracy.
new_findings.expected_impact: Bounds P1's memory/perf downside and predicts the MoE side, not the dense side, as the next thing to break.

The dequant happens inside process_weights_after_loading, so it is a load-time event, not per-step work, and it also removes the activation FP8 requant entirely (input_quant_key() returns None so no manual-fusion pass hoists act-quant upstream of it).

proposal_set.name: gfx90a-fp8-emulation+fresh-compile
proposal_set.reason: Coupled pair, bench as one variant. (1) New default-OFF FP8 w8a8 dense-linear kernel dequantizes the FP8 weight to BF16 ONCE at load time and runs plain F.linear, replacing the ChannelWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel that vLLM selects on gfx90a and that dies in torch._scaled_mm: CDNA2 has no FP8 MMA yet reports capability (9,0), so the Torch kernels' own >=89 arch gate never fires, and the aiter kernels above them are correctly gated off. No config-only route exists - 'emulation' maps only to MXFP4/6/8+NVFP4, 'torch' maps exactly to the three aborting kernels, 'triton' has no ROCm bucket in _LINEAR_BACKEND_KERNEL_MAP so it warns and falls back. (2) VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 is co-required: the AOT artifact hash covers config factors + _model_hash_key(forward) only, and _verify_source_unchanged re-checks just the files the OLD artifact traced, so a registry-only patch never invalidates it - the 17:05 patched boot logged 'Directly load AOT compilation from .../63eba2e7...' and then died on that stale graph's guard assert_size_stride(arg10_1,(4096,2560),(1,4096)) against the now-BF16 [2560,4096] weight. Split them and each half fails: the switch alone hits the stale graph; a fresh compile without the switch reproduces the baseline scaled_mm abort. Blast radius is small and bounded - the dense FP8 volume rewritten is only ~0.29->0.59 GiB per TP rank, the 397B expert weights stay on their own TRITON Fp8 MoE backend.

proposal_set.name: gfx90a-fp8-emulation-forced-via-linear-backend-emulation
proposal_set.reason: Same enablement as P1 plus a deterministic-selection probe, kept atomic because the flag only means something with the patch armed. --linear-backend filters the scaled-MM registry through _resolve_backend_kernels, which falls back to normal selection WITH A WARNING for any layer type the named backend has no kernel for, so it cannot strand MoE (fp8.py:411 picks the TRITON Fp8 MoE backend independently) and cannot strand block-wise dense layers either. Because the patch also registers FP8W8A8EmulationLinearKernel in the emulation bucket, this makes the emulation kernel win by construction instead of by list order - it is the leg to run if P1 boots but P1 s regress, or if a future rebase reshuffles _POSSIBLE_FP8_KERNELS and silently re-selects a Torch kernel. It is NOT expected to beat P1 on throughput: the two differ only in how the winner is chosen, so measure it as a selection-robustness check, not as a gain.

new_findings.what: vLLM 0.28 AOT compile-cache invalidation gap: envs.compile_factors() + VllmConfig.compute_hash() + _model_hash_key(forward) form the artifact dir key, and caching._verify_source_unchanged only re-checks the TRACED files recorded inside the EXISTING artifact. A kernel-selection patch (swap which linear/MoE kernel is chosen, changing weight layout/dtype) touches files that were NEVER in the traced set, so the stale artifact still verifies and is silently replayed -> wrong-shape assert_size_stride in profile_run even though the eager path is correct. Kernel-enablement patches therefore REQUIRE a cold compile.
